It’s been…honestly, I’m not even sure how long now. A while, but the days all blur together since “that day,” as my wife calls it. I know something awful happened, but when I try to think back to it, it’s like hitting a wall. I remember bits and pieces—the sirens, people shouting—but the rest is just…blank. My son keeps asking me what exactly I saw, and I just can’t get most of it back, no matter how hard I try.

What I do know is that anything that even faintly reminds me of it sets me off. A news clip with similar scenes, a sudden loud noise, even a certain smell, and I feel like my chest is going to explode. My heart races, my hands shake, and I just want to get out of there. I’ll switch off the television, leave the room, pretend I’m tired—anything not to think about it.

I’ve started dodging conversations, too. If my family brings it up, I change the subject or say I don’t remember. I spend more time alone in the garden, just to avoid anything that might drag those memories—or whatever’s left of them—back up.
D019-D018_h020.question_a:
About three weeks ago I was in that car crash on the highway. I walked away, but since then I haven’t been myself. 

Whenever I hear screeching brakes or even watch the news and see wrecks, I feel this wave of fear and panic rush over me. My heart races, my hands sweat, and I feel like I’m right back there, even though I can’t really remember the accident properly. It’s strange: I know it happened, people tell me what they saw, but big chunks of it are just… blank. I can’t piece the whole thing together.

I try hard not to think about it. If my wife brings it up, I shut her down or change the subject. I avoid driving past that stretch of road, and I won’t get in the car unless I absolutely have to. When I’m alone, I push the memories away as soon as they start to come up because it feels unbearable.

This has all been going on only since the accident—nothing like this before—and it’s been these last few weeks nonstop.
D019-D018_h020.question_b:

I can recall the screeching sound and seeing headlights, and then nothing clear after that. My wife and the police have filled in the details, but I just can’t seem to piece most of it together, no matter how hard I try.

What I do know is that anything that reminds me of it sets me off. If I hear tires screeching on the street, I freeze up and feel like my chest is tightening. When we pass that intersection, I start sweating and feel panicky. Even watching the news, if there’s a wreck on TV, I have to turn it off immediately.

I go out of my way not to think about it. I avoid driving whenever I can and make excuses so my son or my wife will drive instead. At night, when the house is quiet, I push the thoughts away, because if I let them in, I just feel overwhelmed and can’t settle down. This has been going on steadily since the accident.
